summary.headline: Rallis Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~7% to ₹1,022 cr and EBITDA 23% to ₹184 cr, with growth mostly price-led (~5%) against ~2% volume.
summary.overview: Revenue grew ~7% YoY to ₹1,022 cr, with volume up ~2% and price up ~5%. EBITDA rose 23% to ₹184 cr and PAT rose 31% to ₹125 cr, helped by a ₹35 cr employee-cost provision reversal (₹24 cr described as one-time). Domestic crop protection was the main driver (+19% in Domestic B2C), while exports fell 28% on a 35% volume decline. Management said demand was weak through the quarter because of a delayed monsoon, lagging kharif sowing, cotton acreage loss and channel cash strain from fertilizer buying.

financial_highlights.change: Increase attributed to farmers' fertilizer buying

financial_highlights.value: ₹2 cr profit on sale of property

segments.name: Crop Care
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 7% to ₹697 cr (from ₹652 cr), with volume +2% and price +5%.

segments.name: Domestic B2C (Crop Care)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 19% to ₹534 cr (from ₹449 cr) on 15% volume growth. Crop Protection grew 18% to ₹455 cr on 16% volume growth; Soil & Plant Health grew 10% to ₹62 cr, with price +13%.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Revenue fell 28% to ₹110 cr (from ₹152 cr) on a 35% volume decline, due to weak European pendimethalin demand and Chinese price competition on acephate, Pendi CS and hexaconazole. CSM revenue rose 191% to ₹24 cr on PEKK volume rebound.

segments.name: Total B2B
segments.commentary: Revenue fell 19% to ₹163 cr (from ₹203 cr), with volume down 26%.

segments.name: Seeds
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 6% to ₹325 cr (from ₹305 cr), all from ~6% price growth. Cotton volume fell on North India acreage loss and illegal HTBT cotton, while rice, maize and millet volumes rose. Management said the seed EBITDA margin rose from 26% to 30%, mainly from product mix.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Indian agrochemical market growth of ~6-8% in FY27 and seeds in the mid-to-high single digits excluding cotton, which is expected to decline significantly; the company does not expect cotton seed growth this year.
Price increases were taken earlier in the year; management expects a marginal positive price impact overall, with majority growth to come from volume.
Chilli-related crop protection is expected to recover in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
Long-term target: 500 bps EBITDA margin expansion over five years (set two years ago), and a stated aim to deliver 15%+ EBITDA margin even in a bad year.
Biologicals expected to grow significantly faster than last year; Q1 biologicals grew ~10%.
Plans to launch 3-4 catalogue products in the next three years; CSM ramp-up described as a slow burn.
capex_capacity: Formulation capacity utilisation increased in Q1 FY27 versus Q1 FY26; plant-level numbers to be provided later.
Seed production: company proactively reduced cotton seed production acreage this year; carry-forward cotton seed inventory covers 30-50% of next year's need.

Seed drying: harvest was ~50% larger in some crops; open-field (pad) drying was used because gas-based drying capacity was constrained, which lowered recovery, and the net yield impact is still being calculated.

Launched 4 crop care products (Balwan, Prodim Ultra, Kengen, Aquafert Ginger & Turmeric) and 2 cotton hybrids for North India, HT Direct Seeded Rice (Dhaanya brand) and short-duration bajra; 9 products launched in total across cotton, millet and paddy.
In-licensed a direct-seeded rice technology; pilot sales already made, particularly in Chhattisgarh.
CSM: first shipment made to a US customer; 3-4 further CSM products being worked on.
demand_pricing: Demand was weak in Q1: heatwave, delayed monsoon, farmer crop switching, cotton acreage loss and illegal HTBT cotton spread. Kharif sowing was down ~23% YoY at end-June; by 5 July acreage was still ~21% below last year.
IMD forecasts below-normal monsoon at ~90% of LPA (±4%), with El Niño risk; rainfall was ~15% below normal as of 8 July.

Trade channels diverted cash into fertilizer, causing crop protection cash strain, conservative stocking and slower liquidation. Management said channel inventory had normalised by 21 July after being more worrying a month earlier. Some pre-emergence herbicide returns are expected in Q2.
Pricing: management said most price increases were taken before mid-season; pass-through varied by product, and competitiveness limits how much more can be taken.

Export pricing: Chinese competition is product-specific; acephate is most challenged because its raw material is sourced from the same Chinese producer that competes in Brazil and the US. Pendimethalin, metribuzin, hexaconazole and metalaxyl remain competitive.
Herbicides are now the largest crop protection category; herbicide revenue grew 12% in Q1 (per management).

qa_highlights.question: How are product-wise export demand and pricing trending, given Chinese competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CSM is contract-based and not a challenge, and only catalogue products face pressure, mainly acephate because of its China-sourced raw material. Other products like pendimethalin and hexaconazole remain competitive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for domestic volumes given cotton and the monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects cotton seed to be flat to down for the year; it is pivoting to rice, maize and millet. It said 90-95% of normal cotton area could still deliver a crop-protection outcome similar to last year, but it is too early to predict volumes until mid-August.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further price increases, and how much of the input cost increase has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mid-season price increases are difficult. Pass-through has been full in some products, partial in others and nil in some, and overall price impact is expected to be marginal and positive.

qa_highlights.question: How is working capital and channel inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital is up ~15-20 days YoY, driven by farmers diverting cash to fertilizer. Channel inventory has normalised, and the company is being more cautious on returns provisioning.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the employee cost jump and the ₹35 cr provision reversal?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said ~₹11 cr of the reversal is a recurring Q1 performance-incentive true-up. The remaining ~₹24 cr relates to restructuring and retirement items and is one-time. Underlying cost growth is ~12%, in line with inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 6-8% agrochemical and mid-to-high single-digit seed growth estimates realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said these are excluding cotton. It expects the price increase to deliver the 6-8% growth, as demand and supply appear balanced and there is no sign of panic discounting.

risks_watch: Monsoon and El Niño: below-normal rainfall risk for the second half of the season, and possible crop-protection volume shortfall.
Channel cash and returns: elevated sales returns risk, and higher returns provisioning; management said it cannot yet estimate the total return amount.
Export competition from China, mainly acephate, and weak European and Brazilian demand.
Input-cost volatility: crude, freight and Middle East conflict could raise rabi input costs; management said rabi procurement starts in August.
Working capital: up ~15-20 days YoY, with inventory elevated versus last year.
Seed cotton inventory and HTBT cotton spread; seed drying and recovery economics still being calculated.
Employee cost and other expenses rising (other expenses up ~13-14%); management says some items are one-time.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the brand, portfolio and medium-term margin path, but cautious on the near-term volume outlook, which management says depends on the monsoon. Management was evasive on specific return amounts, channel inventory figures and capacity-utilisation numbers, deferring them to follow-ups.
key_quotes: So we want to be a consistent company, which delivers 15% plus EBITDA margin even in a bad year.
The key takeaway is that costs remained elevated while demand recovery was insufficient to support price hikes, resulting in continued margin stress across the sector.

Majority of the growth has to come from volume, and that's where your market excellence, your ability to work with the dealers, distributors, farmers generate demand, be very agile on positioning stocks in the market, all of those factors will come to play.

growth.why: Management expects Indian agrochemical market growth of ~6-8% in FY27 with a marginal positive price impact and majority of growth from volume, backed by product launches, biologicals and chilli recovery in Q2-Q3, but no specific capacity or order numbers were given and the brief shows weak Q1 demand and a delayed monsoon.
